title: Lentiviral-mediated ectopic expression of YAP and TAZ in YAPoff cancer cell lines
protocol: Transfect packaging cells for each transfer plasmid (e.g., YAP or TAZ) using 3 × 10 cm plates per virus type.
Collect viral supernatant from transfected cells.
Concentrate the collected viral supernatant by high-speed centrifugation.
Seed approximately 4 × 10^6 Lenti-X 293T cells per plate into 18 × 10 cm plates the day prior to transfection.
Aspirate media from Lenti-X 293T cells and replace with 8 mL of DMEM + 10% FBS (without antibiotics).
Prepare a transfection mixture using two sterile tubes per transfection, one for plasmid DNA and one for FuGENE HD transfection reagent.
Mix the plasmid DNA in Tube 1 according to Table 1 specifications.
Dilute FuGENE HD transfection reagent with media in Tube 2 as specified.
Incubate both mixtures approximately 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Combine the contents of Tube 1 and Tube 2, pipette to mix thoroughly.
Incubate the combined mixture for 10–15 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Add 500 μL of transfection mixture dropwise to each 10 cm plate of Lenti-X 293T cells.
Gently swirl the plates after adding the transfection mixture.
Incubate the cells for 12–18 hours.
Replace the media on packaging cells with 10 mL of DMEM + 10% FBS (without antibiotics).
Incubate the cells for an additional 36–48 hours.
Collect and concentrate lentivirus by high-speed centrifugation inside a BSC.
Place an open-top thin wall ultra-clear round bottom tube into each bucket of a JS-24.38 swinging bucket rotor.
Collect lentivirus-containing media from Lenti-X 293T cells and combine up to 30 mL in a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the collected media at 500 g for 5 minutes to remove large debris.
Filter up to 30 mL of supernatant directly into the centrifuge bucket using a 0.45 μm low protein binding syringe filter attached to a 30 cc Luer-Lok syringe.
Underlay 4 mL of 20% sucrose (in PBS) underneath the virus-containing media to create a sucrose cushion and tightly seal the rotor bucket.
Weigh each bucket and adjust volumes to balance the buckets, keeping them within 0.05 g of one another using DMEM + 10% FBS if needed.
Tightly seal the rotor buckets and load the buckets onto the JS-24.38 rotor.
Secure the rotor into the Avanti J-30I high-performance centrifuge.
Centrifuge for ≥2 h at 4°C and max speed of 24,000 rpm (∼103,000 g) with settings “SLOW” for ACCEL and DECEL.
Remove buckets from the centrifuge immediately upon stopping and transport to a biological safety cabinet.
Unscrew bucket lids carefully using sterile forceps.
Carefully remove round bottom tubes and place them in a rack with opening facing up after decanting supernatant and allowing excess media to drain.
Add 300 μL of sterile, cold PBS to the bottom of each tube.
Adjust the pipette volume to ∼200 μL to avoid bubbles/frothing.
Pipette up and down ∼2 min to resuspend the virus.
Mix tubes containing different viruses together if applicable.
Prepare appropriately sized aliquots of the virus into sterile tubes.
Store virus aliquots at −80°C.
Avoid multiple freeze-thaw cycles to maintain viral titer.
Transfer confluent NCI-H209 cells to a conical tube.
Centrifuge cells at 300 g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant from the centrifuged cells.
Resuspend cells back to their original volume in culture media.
Pipette cells vigorously to ensure a single cell suspension.
Count cells using a hemocytometer or other counting method.
Dilute cells to a concentration of 5 × 10^5 cells/mL.
Add Polybrene to the cell suspension to achieve a final concentration of 4 μg/mL.
Transfer 500 μL of the cell suspension (2.5 × 10^5 cells) to separate wells of a 24-well tissue culture plate.
Thaw an aliquot of each virus stock.
Prepare five, 3-fold serial dilutions of each virus into PBS.
Add 2.5 μL from each dilution to separate wells of the 24-well plate.
Incubate the cells with virus for 14–18 hours.
Collect cells using a P1000 pipette.
Pipette up and down 2–3 times to remove loosely attached cells.
Transfer collected cells to a sterile microfuge tube.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 minutes at 800 g.
Carefully remove the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 750 μL of media.
Transfer the cells to a new 24-well plate.
Incubate the cells for 3–4 days.
Calculate viral titer after 3–4 days in culture (4–5 days after viral transduction).
Stain the cells for GFP expression using flow cytometry.
Assess GFP fluorescence using a fluorescent microscope if necessary.
Prepare NCI-H209 cells for transduction.
Transduce 2 × 10^6 NCI-H209 cells with lentivirus at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of approximately 4.
Incubate the cells with the viral solution to allow transduction.
Monitor GFP expression over time using a fluorescent microscope.
Assess YAP/TAZ/GFP expression as soon as it plateaus, typically 4-5 days after transduction.
Harvest and count cells as described in steps 5a–5c.
Add Polybrene to a final concentration of 4 μg/mL.
Transfer 4 mL of cell suspension (2 × 10^6 cells) to separate wells of a 6-well tissue culture plate.
Prepare one well for each virus to be used plus one additional well for a non-transduced control.
Thaw viral aliquots and add the appropriate volume of Empty vector control or individual YAP/TAZ viruses to achieve MOI of ∼4 (e.g., 8 × 10^6 viral particles).
Gently swirl plate to mix.
Incubate cells 14–18 hours.
Collect cells and transfer to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Wash cells once in culture media.
Resuspend the cells in 6 mL of fresh culture media.
Transfer the resuspended cells to a T25 tissue culture flask.
Incubate for 4 days.
Monitor cell density and passage or supplement with additional media if necessary.
Transduce NCI-H209 cells with YAP/TAZ lentiviruses.
Use Beckman Coulter Gallios flow cytometer for analyzing GFP and YAP/TAZ expression in transduced cells.
Include non-transduced NCI-H209 cells as a negative control for both GFP and YAP/TAZ expression.
Use Empty vector cell line as a single-stained (GFP+/YAP-) control.
Consider including additional unstained and single antibody-stained controls initially until experience is gained with the techniques.
Harvest and fix cells.
Collect control YAPon cell line by trypsination and transfer 0.5–1.0 × 10^6 cells to each of two different 1.5 mL microfuge tubes.
Transfer 0.5–1.0 × 10^6 transduced or control NCI-H209 cells to separate 1.5 mL microfuge tubes.
Centrifuge cells at 800 g for 5 min in a table-top microfuge, discard the supernatant and wash the cells once with 1 mL of PBS.
Resuspend the cells in 250 μL of 4% PFA, and incubate 10–15 min at 20°C–25°C.
Centrifuge cells at 800 g for 5 min at 4°C, discard the supernatant and wash the cells twice with 1 mL of PBS.
Store cells in 500 μl of PBS at 4°C for up to 1 week.
Pellet cells as before and remove old PBS prior to continuing.
Resuspend cells in 500 μL of perm/block buffer.
Transfer the suspension to a new 1.5 mL microfuge tube.
Incubate at 20°C–25°C for 30 minutes.
Invert tubes 2–3 times after approximately 15 minutes.
Centrifuge cells at 800 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Very carefully remove the supernatant using a P1000 pipette.
Resuspend cells in 100–200 μL of primary antibody diluted in stain/wash buffer, or stain/wash buffer alone for unstained controls.
Incubate cells for 1 hour at 20°C–25°C.
Gently flick the tube to resuspend cells every 15 minutes.
Add 1 mL of stain/wash buffer to each sample and centrifuge as before.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Wash cells once more with 1 mL stain/wash buffer.
Resuspend cells in 100–200 μL of secondary antibodies diluted 1:750 in stain/wash buffer.
Incubate cells for 30 minutes at 20°C–25°C, protected from light.
Gently flick the tube to resuspend cells after approximately 15 minutes.
Add 1 mL of stain/wash buffer to each sample and centrifuge as before.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Wash cells once more with 1 mL stain/wash buffer.
Resuspend cells in 300 μL of FACS buffer.
Filter the cell suspension through a cell strainer cap affixed to a FACS tube.
Analyze samples immediately on Beckman Coulter Gallios flow cytometer using Kaluza analysis software.
Alternatively, store filtered samples at 4°C for up to 24 hours before analysis.
Prepare protein lysates ensuring lysis buffer is ice cold.
Maintain cells and protein lysates on ice during processing.
Perform all centrifugation steps at 4°C.
Harvest a portion of transduced NCI-H209 cells similarly to specified steps.
Harvest control YAPon cells (e.g., NCI-H661) in the same manner.
Pellet cells by centrifugation.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellets in 1 mL of PBS.
Transfer resuspended cells to a 1.5 mL microfuge tube.
Prepare RIPA lysis buffer with Protease/Phosphatase inhibitor cocktail and PMSF at a 1:100 dilution.
Add 100 μL of cold lysis buffer to each cell pellet.
Pipette to fully resuspend the pellet.
Incubate samples on ice for 5 min.
Sonicate samples 2 × 3 s with a 3 s pause between using a Fisher Scientific Model 100 Sonic Dismembrator at setting “4” (power output ∼12 W).
If sonicator is unavailable, increase incubation time to 10 min without sonication.
Centrifuge samples for 10 min at 4°C and ≥ 16,000 g.
Transfer supernatants (protein lysate) to pre-chilled microfuge tubes.
Store protein lysates long term at −80°C or thaw on ice if previously frozen.
Determine protein concentration using the Bio-Rad Protein Assay Kit II.
Dilute 5 μL of lysate or lysis buffer alone 1:10 in dH2O.
Prepare BSA standards as outlined in the manufacturer’s protocol.
Add 10 μL of standard or sample to separate wells of a 96-well plate in duplicate or triplicate.
Add 200 μL of diluted reagent and incubate for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Read absorbance at 595 nm using a microplate reader.
Prepare a standard curve plotting the absorbance versus concentration of BSA standards.
Determine the concentration of each sample by linear regression.
Multiply the determined concentration by 10 to account for the initial dilution.
Dilute a portion of each sample using RIPA lysis buffer so that samples are of equal concentration, such as 2 μg/μL.
Dilute protein lysates 1:1 with 2× Laemmli sample buffer.
Heat diluted samples at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Allow heated samples to cool to 20°C–25°C and briefly centrifuge.
Remove pre-cast SDS-PAGE gel from packaging.
Assemble electrophoresis apparatus.
Fill chambers with Tris-Glycine-SDS running buffer.
Remove comb from the gel and flush wells with a P200 pipette set to ∼30 μL.
Mix 3 μL of PageRuler Prestained protein marker with 7 μL of 1× Laemmli sample buffer.
Load mixed marker into lane 1 of the gel.
Load 10–25 μg of protein lysate from each sample onto subsequent wells.
For any empty wells, load 10 μL of 1× Laemmli sample buffer.
Attach lid onto the electrophoresis unit and connect to power supply.
Run at constant amperage of 30 mA/gel (for mini gels) or 70 mA/gel (for midi gels).
Maintain a maximum voltage of 200 V for ∼1 h until the blue dye front runs off the end of the gel.
Turn power unit off and remove gel(s).
Separate plates and gently cut off the top of the gel where the wells were.
Carefully transfer the gel(s) to a reservoir containing 1× transfer buffer.
Briefly equilibrate one nitrocellulose membrane per gel in transfer buffer.
Wet two transfer stacks per gel.
Assemble "transfer sandwich" by placing one transfer stack in the bottom of the Trans-Blot Turbo cassette.
Place the nitrocellulose membrane on the transfer stack and align sides.
Place the gel on top of the membrane.
Add the last transfer stack on top of the gel.
Gently roll out to remove bubbles.
Carefully dab away excess buffer.
Place the cassette lid on top and turn dial to lock in place.
Turn on the Trans-Blot Turbo instrument using the switch located near the back.
Slide the assembled cassette into slot "A" or "B" of the instrument.
Select "LIST" using the control panel buttons.
Select "BIO-RAD" using the right-hand side buttons.
Choose either "1 MINI GEL" or "2 MINI OR 1 MIDI GEL" as appropriate.
Scroll down until "MIXED MW" is highlighted and select "RUN".
Either “A:RUN” or “B:RUN” using the bottom set of buttons on the display depending whether the cassette is located in slot A or B.
Turn off the instrument after transfer is complete.
Remove the cassette and then remove the cassette lid.
Discard the top transfer stack from the transfer sandwich.
Lift the gel from the side containing the protein marker, ensuring the marker has properly transferred to the membrane.
Place the membrane in a container with 20–30 mL of 5% milk and incubate for 1–2 hours at 20°C–25°C or overnight at 4°C.
Rinse the membrane briefly in 0.1% TBS-T.
Add YAP/TAZ primary antibody diluted 1:500 in 1× TBS to cover the membrane (∼10 mL for a mini gel) and incubate for 1 hour at 20°C–25°C then overnight at 4°C.
Remove the primary antibody (can be stored at 4°C and reused).
Wash the membrane with 3 × 10 minutes in 0.1% TBS-T.
Add goat anti-mouse IRDye 680RD diluted 1:5000 in 0.1% TBS-T to cover the membrane (∼10–15 mL) and incubate for 1 hour at 20°C–25°C, protected from light.
Wash the membrane with 3 × 10 minutes in 0.1% TBS-T.
Image using a LI-COR Odyssey Infrared imaging system according to manufacturer’s protocols.
Quantify band intensities for YAP and/or TAZ using the LI-COR Odyssey software.
Ensure bands are not saturated after scanning; indicated by a blue color, re-scan at a lower “Intensity” if necessary.
Strip membrane in 15–20 mL of TBS, pH 2.0 for 1–2 h at 20°C–25°C.
Wash membrane 3 × 10 min with ∼15 mL of 0.1% TBS-T.
Add primary anti-TUBULIN antibody (Santa Cruz Biotechnology, clone DM1A diluted 1:2000 in TBS).
Incubate at 4°C for 14–24 h.
Repeat steps to image and quantify TUBULIN band intensities.
